messages:
marta: APAC region reporting a sharp p95/p99 latency spike on runtime (na-apac1). Starting investigation, looks related to KV cache churn + thin GPU hotpool capacity.
raj: seeing p95 go from ~180ms -> 1.4s and p99 up to ~3.8s since 1950001180. Error rate on hotpool allocations increased, evictions spiked.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] region: apac, metric: runtime_latency_p95, value: 1400ms, threshold: 300ms
runtime-eng: I think the continuous-batcher change from the last deploy is pushing bigger batch windows -> KV cache pressure for long contexts. Opening runtime PR link: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4789 (deployed at 1950001100).
infra-engineer: hotpool utilization is at 96% and we have thin provisioning in that cluster (auto-scale cooldown long). GPU pod OOM/kvcache eviction logs showing LRU churn.
raj: also noticed a routing wobble: smart-routing is attempting region fallback to na1 which is adding 160-320ms per request and increasing egress cost.
runtime-eng: immediate mitigation: disable continuous batching on apac nodes and drop target batch size from 16 -> 4 for affected model routes. That should reduce KV cache tail pressure.
infra-engineer: running scale action now: `redwood infra scale-hotpool --region apac --add 6-gpus --priority emergency` to add capacity. ETA ~120s for pods to register.
deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime rollback toggle -> disable-continuous-batching flag (operator). Job id: deploy-1950001252
raj: temporary traffic shift to na1 for lower-priority tenants is active (route policy: apac->na1 low-priority) to offload hotpool. Monitoring cost/latency.
cost-ops: heads up — cross-region traffic will add egress costs. Rough estimate: if traffic shift holds we may see an incremental of ~$6-10k/hr depending on sustained throughput.
sre-lead: prioritize customer-impacting routes. No full region failover unless hotpool scale and runtime mitigations don't help in 10m. Postmortem required.
marta: applied `disable-continuous-batching` and batch size override. Early signals: p95 dropped to ~310ms at 1950001290. kvcache eviction rate down by ~60%.
runtime-eng: confirming: trace sample shows fewer cross-pod KV fetches and lower tail latency. We'll revert the PR change in next patch and run canary.
infra-engineer: hotpool scale completed, nodes registering. Hotpool reclaim is still aggressive due to thinpool config; filing follow-up to increase min-reserve for apac.
raj: users seeing fewer timeouts, but some background jobs still hitting older connections. We should gracefully drain old pods.
marta: draining old pods now: `kubectl cordon && kubectl drain --grace-period=30s` on affected nodes.
sre-lead: good work. Action items: 1) roll back runtime PR, 2) increase hotpool min-reserve for apac, 3) add autoscaler cooldown tweak, 4) update routing policy to prefer local fallback before cross-region for latency-sensitive tenants.
cost-ops: will rerun cost model after 1hr window and propose throttles for non-critical workloads to limit spend.
raj: capturing logs/graphs and will create incident page with timeline + commands used.
marta: creating incident doc and tagging postmortem. PR link that likely caused regression: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4789.
sre-lead: we held service; no customer data loss. Postmortem expectations: root cause, why thinpool min-reserve was low, why continuous-batcher flag shipped without perf canary.
marta: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with follow-ups and the incident doc link when ready.
metadata: severity: high, incident_type: region_degradation, mitigation: scale_hotpool/disable_batching/traffic_shift, followups: rollback_pr/increase_reserve/postmortem
